blocks.text:
Day 4  ·  Breakfast. Excursion to the Perito Moreno Glacier in Los Glaciares National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site whose 47 glaciers reveal a cold, wild world. The Perito Moreno, in the south-west of Lago Argentino, 80 km from El Calafate, is named after a great 19th-century Argentine explorer and is one of the few glaciers in the world that is not retreating, which makes it one of the most spectacular sights in South America. From time to time its 60-metre ice front releases walls of ice the size of buildings into Brazo Rico or the Canal de los Témpanos (Iceberg Channel), where they float away across the lake.

Every four to six years, the advancing glacier reaches the Magallanes Peninsula on the opposite shore and divides the lake in two: Brazo Rico is dammed and rises some 35 metres above its usual level, until its waters slowly carve through the ice and the barrier collapses. A breathtaking sight.

blocks.text: Day 5  ·  After breakfast, transfer from your hotel in El Calafate to Puerto Natales, crossing the vast Patagonian steppe towards the Chilean border, through striking landscapes of mountain peaks, wide plains and wind-shaped hills, where you may see guanacos, foxes, rheas (ñandú) and hares. After the border formalities, continue through remote Chilean Patagonia to Puerto Natales, a quiet and charming town on the shores of the Última Esperanza (Last Hope) Sound, gateway to Torres del Paine National Park. Transfer to the hotel; the rest of the day is at leisure.
